newsitem.title: USA: Neb voters approve $89 mln school bond referendum.
newsitem.headline: Neb voters approve $89 mln school bond referendum.

text.p: Voters in a growing suburban Omaha, Neb., school district approved an $89 million school bond referendum Tuesday for renovation, new construction and technological improvements, the district planning director said Wednesday.
Voters passed the referendum for Millard Public Schools, southwest of Omaha, by a 52 percent to 48 percent margin, planning director John Crawford said.
The district plans to issue the debt over three years, with $30 million of bonds in September, another $30 million in September 1998 and $29 million in September 1999, Crawford said.
The district plans to spend $49.8 million for improvements to existing buildings and another $27.8 million for construction of two elementary school buildings and a middle school, Crawford said.
Another $7.3 million will be spent on computers for the district and about $4.1 million for design and related expenses, Crawford said.
District officials estimated that the referendum would raise property taxes $94 per year for a $100,000 home, Crawford said.
